title: Faithful reading
statement: Reproduce what the source prints, as exactly as the encoding allows. A transcription reads; it does not edit.

title: Meaning over appearance
statement: Encode musical meaning in a form that converts, plays back and survives tool changes. Where an exact visual copy conflicts with a standard encoding, use the standard encoding, only through the registered normalisations, and report them.

title: Judgement stays out
statement: Do not choose between readings, correct, complete or interpret. A transcription records; judgement belongs elsewhere.

title: In doubt, preserve
statement: When it is unclear which tier a decision falls in, treat it as editorial. Keep what the source prints, flag the point and ask a reviewer.

title: Preserve the distinctions the source makes
statement: Where the source uses different notations for what might seem the same, keep the difference (for example common time, cut time and 4/4; ties and slurs; acciaccatura and appoggiatura; key signatures as given).

title: Consistency means equivalence only
statement: Encode notations that mean the same thing the same way. Preserve any divergence that might be musical (a different articulation in one part, a different pitch in a repeated passage); do not harmonise it.

title: Source errors are preserved
statement: Transcribe an evident source error as printed and flag it for whoever maintains corrections. Never fix it silently in the transcription.

title: Record the source's own editorial marks
statement: Brackets and similar marks printed in the source signal an intervention by that edition. Keep the element, record each such mark in the report, and drop the printed mark from the encoding only if the standard encoding requires it.

title: Transcribe every printed mark
statement: Transcribe pitches, rhythms and every printed mark, within what the encoding can express. A category of mark that is classed as editorial or unsupported (see mark_categories; a profile may reclassify a category) is left out systematically and stated once in each report.

title: Keep the source language
statement: Keep musical terms and other text in the source language. Translations are additions.

title: Standard encodings for instructions
statement: Transcribe printed techniques, strings, mutes and harmonics using the standard encoding where one exists, even where that changes the printed wording.

title: Preserve composer-led grouping
statement: Preserve beaming, rest and similar grouping that carries musical meaning (the composer's own choice for a passage). Grouping that is only the source edition's habit is a presentation matter. If the two cannot be told apart, ask a reviewer and report the decision.

title: Ornaments as printed
statement: Copy ornaments as printed, including the difference between acciaccatura and appoggiatura and the position before or after the main note. Where the tool cannot represent a detail, use the nearest available form in this order - type of ornament, then number of beams or strokes, then other indications.

title: Real objects, not drawings or text
statement: Encode ties, slurs, hairpins, spanning lines, tuplets, tremolo and grace notes as the musical objects they are, so that playback and export work. Do not draw them or type them as text.

title: Defaults, not manual overrides
statement: Use the tool's defaults for placement, stem direction, accidentals and similar. Avoid manual position offsets and flips.

title: Source layout is removable data
statement: Record the source's system and page breaks where possible, never split a bar across them, and keep them separable from the musical content so that they can be removed in one step. Where a source has no usable layout, omit them and say so.

title: Normalisations are a closed list
statement: Presentation normalisations are limited to those registered in this domain. A profile chooses which are permitted or required; local notes may not add to them. Each applied normalisation is stated once per transcription in the report.

title: Beam grouping
statement: Beam grouping follows the time-signature default, except where grouping is composer-led.

title: Rest grouping
statement: Rest grouping follows the time-signature default, except where grouping is composer-led.

title: Tuplet brackets
statement: Tuplet brackets use a single standard form. Repeated tuplet numbers in a long group may be hidden but are kept in the data.

title: Tremolo
statement: A measured tremolo may use any semantically equivalent notation.

title: Stem and placement
statement: Stem direction and similar placement is automatic.

title: Accidental conventions
statement: Courtesy accidentals and cancelling naturals follow the default.

title: Clefs
statement: An unusual or obsolete clef may be replaced by its nearest modern equivalent; an octave-ambiguous clef is notated at sounding pitch; a brief clef change may be adapted for readability. Written pitch is unaffected.

title: Standard terms and abbreviations
statement: Standard abbreviations and equivalent terms are normalised (for example one standard form for decrescendo and diminuendo); anything ambiguous is spelled out.

title: Words spread over several bars
statement: A word spread over several bars or systems (for example cre - - scen - - do) is one spanning object with a start text and a continuation text.

title: Page geometry and typography
statement: Page geometry and typography follow defaults. The source's system and page breaks are kept as data.

title: Additions are rare and marked
statement: Add only what is needed to express the source's own notational conventions in the encoding (for example accidentals that the source's convention leaves implicit). Mark every addition visibly. Translations of non-standard terms are additions. Anything that needs judgement is editorial, not an addition.

title: Report every unmarked deviation
statement: Report every deviation that is not visibly marked. Differences caused by registered normalisations are stated once per transcription; specific interventions are listed one by one. The report, with the transcription, is enough to recover what the source prints.

title: Record provenance
statement: Record the source edition and file, the pages where the transcription appears, who transcribed and reviewed it, when, which tools were used, and the versions of the Principles, profile and notes applied.
